structuring.name: Structuring / CTR Avoidance
structuring.description: Repeated transactions are deliberately kept below a reporting threshold within a short window to reduce the chance of mandatory reporting.

cash_withdrawal.name: Rapid Cash Withdrawal
cash_withdrawal.description: Funds are withdrawn in cash soon after receipt, limiting retention time and weakening the transaction trail.
cash_withdrawal.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

deposit_send.name: Deposit Then Send
deposit_send.description: A new deposit is followed by a rapid outbound transfer, producing unusually high short-window transaction velocity.
deposit_send.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

smurfing.name: Smurfing
smurfing.description: Multiple senders coordinate smaller transactions that converge on a beneficiary, obscuring the aggregate value and source of funds.

layered_fan_in.name: Layered Fan-In
layered_fan_in.description: Funds pass through intermediary accounts before many transaction paths converge on a smaller set of recipients.
layered_fan_in.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

layered_fan_out.name: Layered Fan-Out
layered_fan_out.description: Funds pass through intermediaries and then disperse from a small number of accounts to many recipients.
layered_fan_out.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

stacked_bipartite.name: Stacked Bipartite Transfers
stacked_bipartite.description: Multiple layers of sender and receiver groups form repeated many-to-many transfer structures.
stacked_bipartite.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

behavioural_change_1.name: Behavioural Change Type 1
behavioural_change_1.description: An account's transaction amounts or frequency move sharply away from its established historical behaviour.
behavioural_change_1.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

bipartite.name: Bipartite Transfer Pattern
bipartite.description: Two groups of accounts exhibit dense or coordinated transfers across the groups with limited activity within each group.
bipartite.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

cycle.name: Circular / Round-Trip Transfers
cycle.description: Funds move through a directed chain and return to an earlier account, creating a circular flow that can obscure origin.
cycle.reg_ref: FATF trade-based money laundering guidance; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

fan_in.name: Fan-In
fan_in.description: Many source accounts send funds to a common beneficiary in a concentrated time window.
fan_in.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

gather_scatter.name: Gather-Scatter
gather_scatter.description: Funds from multiple sources gather in one or more hubs and are subsequently dispersed to multiple recipients.
gather_scatter.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

behavioural_change_2.name: Behavioural Change Type 2
behavioural_change_2.description: An account develops a second form of material deviation from its normal amount distribution or payment behaviour.
behavioural_change_2.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

scatter_gather.name: Scatter-Gather
scatter_gather.description: Funds first disperse through multiple accounts and later reconverge, introducing layers between source and destination.
scatter_gather.reg_ref: FATF 40 Recommendations; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

single_large.name: Single Large Transaction
single_large.description: A single unusually large transaction is inconsistent with the account or peer baseline and warrants contextual review.
single_large.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

fan_out.name: Fan-Out
fan_out.description: One source account distributes funds to many destination accounts in a concentrated period.
fan_out.reg_ref: FATF Recommendation 20; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

over_invoicing.name: Over-Invoicing
over_invoicing.description: A payment may materially exceed the expected value of the represented goods or services and requires documentary review.
over_invoicing.reg_ref: FATF trade-based money laundering guidance; SAML-D synthetic typology taxonomy

normal_small_fan_out.name: Normal Small Fan-Out
normal_small_fan_out.description: Legitimate low-value distributions to a small set of recipients, used as a negative graph baseline.

normal_fan_out.name: Normal Fan-Out
normal_fan_out.description: Legitimate recurring distributions to multiple recipients, used to distinguish benign fan-out activity.

normal_fan_in.name: Normal Fan-In
normal_fan_in.description: Legitimate receipts from multiple sources, used to distinguish benign fan-in activity.

normal_group.name: Normal Group Activity
normal_group.description: Routine transfers within a legitimate account group, used as a negative network baseline.

normal_cash_withdrawal.name: Normal Cash Withdrawal
normal_cash_withdrawal.description: Routine cash withdrawals that establish a baseline for amount and frequency comparisons.

normal_cash_deposits.name: Normal Cash Deposits
normal_cash_deposits.description: Routine cash deposits that establish a baseline for deposit amount and cadence.

normal_periodical.name: Normal Periodical Activity
normal_periodical.description: Legitimate transactions occurring on a regular schedule, used as a cadence baseline.

normal_plus_mutual.name: Normal Plus Mutual Activity
normal_plus_mutual.description: Legitimate mixed activity that includes reciprocal transfers, used as a negative graph baseline.

normal_mutual.name: Normal Mutual Transfers
normal_mutual.description: Legitimate reciprocal transfers between accounts, used to avoid treating all two-way flows as suspicious.

normal_forward.name: Normal Forward Transfers
normal_forward.description: Legitimate onward transfers represented by the source label's original spelling, used as a negative flow baseline.

normal_single_large.name: Normal Single Large Transaction
normal_single_large.description: Legitimate large-value activity used to prevent an amount threshold alone from determining suspicion.
